card.title: ANDERS' ARMY
card.text: Draw 2 cards. Deal 2 damage to your HQ.
card.flavorText: Anders’ Army was the common name for the Polish Armed Forces in the East, formed in the Soviet Union in 1941 under General Władysław Anders. Its ranks came largely from Polish citizens released from Soviet captivity after the Sikorski-Mayski agreement restored relations between the Soviet Union and the Polish government-in-exile. Many recruits arrived weak from imprisonment, hunger, and forced displacement, yet they became the core of a new Polish force. The army first organized around Buzuluk and Totskoye, then expanded in Central Asia. By late 1941 it counted around 25,000 soldiers, but shortages of food, clothing, weapons and transport made training difficult. Polish civilians, including soldiers’ families and orphans, gathered around the camps and shared the same hardship. In 1942, Anders’ Army was evacuated through the Caspian Sea and overland routes into Iran. About 79,000 soldiers and 37,000 civilians left the Soviet Union. The army then moved through Iran, Iraq, and Palestine under British command. Many of its soldiers later formed the Polish II Corps, which fought in Italy, notably at Monte Cassino.
